children: Uruguay’s GDP declined 0.5% year over year in the second quarter of 2026.

The agriculture, fisheries and mining sectors contracted 22.2%, reflecting a poor soybean yield in the 2025/2026 harvest season due to drought, as well as a challenging comparison with the previous season, which ended with a historically high yield.
Manufacturing grew 1.9%, driven by stronger cellulose pulp production.
Trade, accommodation, and food and beverage services increased 2.8%, supported by the performance of the trade sector.
Construction grew 4.2%, driven by increased investment in both nonresidential buildings and other construction projects.

title: Uruguay Economy Shrinks in Q2 2026
